Subject: Operator console license matrix and platform fee amortization

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the low-latency routing and the KV cache stuff. We’re starting to pull together procurement docs and Clarify needs a clearer view on how Redwood is planning to price the private operator console / management plane for an air-gapped VPC deployment. Specifically: 

- How do you license the operator/management plane vs. the inference nodes? We need a per-node license + an operator seat model or similar.
- Is the platform fee (the recurring platform/console charge) amortized if we take an annual committed capacity? Clarify’s finance team wants to amortize over 36 months for capex scheduling.
- What are the support tiers, response times, and on-call windows for on-prem? We need a clear SLO matrix to feed into our security and procurement (SOC 2 will be required).

I attached Appendix B from our RFP (Clarify_RFP_Appendix_B.pdf) and a quick license comparison (License_Matrix_2x2.xlsx). Can you send an initial pricing/packaging proposal that calls out: node license, operator console seats, platform fee options (monthly vs. amortized annually), and proposed discounts for a 3-year commit?

Looking for something we can show our CFO next Wednesday (2026-12-08).

Thanks,
Sara

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jin <sara.jin@clarifyhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Operator console license matrix and platform fee amortization

Sara,

Appreciate the materials — that appendix is helpful. High level answer first, then a compact pricing sketch for the CFO: 

Summary (short):
- Licensing: inference nodes licensed per active GPU host (soft cap on cores/nodes); operator/management plane licensed per "operator seat" (concurrent admin sessions) with a small cluster-level entitlement for automation.
- Platform fee: charged as a recurring subscription (monthly/annual). For committed 3-year deals we can amortize and offer a tranche credit applied to the platform fee with annual accounting-friendly invoices.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 8x5), Priority (24x7 phone triage + 2hr P1 response), and Enterprise (dedicated on-call, 1hr P1, quarterly runbooks & audit assistance). SOC 2 artifacts can be delivered and we offer an additional compliance bundle to speed audits.

Initial pricing sketch (ballpark numbers to align expectations):
- Node license: $1,200 / GPU-host / month (list).
- Operator seat: $400 / seat / month (concurrent).
- Platform fee: $4,000 / month for cluster management + $0.02 / inference-hour metering (meter optional).

3-year commit offer (examples):
A) Conservative: 15% discount on node license; platform fee amortized with a 12-month upfront credit (equivalent to ~8% effective discount).
B) Aggressive: 25% discount on node license + 2 operator seats included + platform fee credited by 20% in year 1 for migration/support.

Items to confirm for formal quote: expected steady-state GPU count, peak burst needs, expected concurrent operator seats, and whether the deployment must be air-gapped / fully offline (that raises packaging/transport costs).

I’m attaching our internal SKU sheet (Redwood_Operator_Pricing_SKU_v1.xlsx) for reference. I can convert the sketch into a formal SOW and commercial term sheet if these numbers look directionally right.

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-04T10:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Operator console license matrix and platform fee amortization — need approval on negotiation levers

Avery —

We can be flexible. Margin floor and operational assumptions below: 

- Margin floor: we need to preserve ~62% gross margin on node-license revenue for on-prem (includes packaging/transportation/support uplift). That means the node discount floor is ~18% for a 3-year commit.
- Platform fee: we can offer a migration credit equivalent to 3 months platform fee in year 1 for a 3-year commit. If they want full amortization over 36 months we can structure invoices as annual with an accounting credit but the cash will be recognized on our side per normal ARR rules.
- Operator seats: include 2 seats for free at signing for up to 12 months. Additional seats at $300/month thereafter.
- Support uplift for Enterprise (dedicated on-call): $15k / month (covers 1 FTE fractional rotation + tooling/incident ops cost).

Acceptable negotiation playbook: start at Aggressive (25% node, 2 included seats, 20% platform fee credit Y1) but build in a mid-year price step if they underutilize. If procurement pushes for more, we can trade infra-start credits (implementation hours) not price.

Approve sending a formal term sheet with those terms.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference

On support note: Karthik — please confirm if $15k/month covers on-call + quarterly runbook updates. If not, give a revised number and I’ll update the SOW.

Avery,

Thanks — Clarify’s CFO reviewed your sketch and the playbook and we’re comfortable moving forward on the following high-level commercial guardrails: 

- 3-year commit, target steady-state of 18 GPU hosts (with expected seasonal burst up to 24).
- Node license at 20% discount (mid between conservative/aggressive) for years 1–3, with utilization-based stepped pricing if average utilization falls below 40% in Y2.
- Platform fee: apply migration credit equal to 3 months in Y1; Redwood will provide an annual invoice schedule that Clarify can amortize over 36 months internally.
- Operator seats: 2 seats included for 12 months; additional seats at $300/month.
- Support: Priority tier (24x7 triage + 2hr P1) is acceptable; Clarify may upgrade to Enterprise after 12 months.

Please send a short SOW and a DocuSign term sheet reflecting these points. We'll aim to get procurement signatures the week of 2027-01-04. Also include a short appendix describing SOC 2 evidence delivery timelines and an exportable audit log sample.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
